relations: As the osprey beats its raised wings upward, water is displaced into a spreading spray around its body.
When wing-generated lift exceeds the bird's weight, its body begins rising out of the water surface.
As the bird clears the surface, water droplets shed from its wet feathers and tail.
The ripples from the splash expand outward across the calm water after the body leaves it.
